title: PostgreSQL backup and recovery with pgBackRest

release.label: HA001 owner release — verified AWS workflow and authenticated UI

steps.title: Understand recoverability with pgBackRest
steps.workplace_problem: An accidental update has reached both the database and its standby. The backup dashboard is green. Can you recover the right business records, prove them, and return the service safely?
learning_outcomes: Explain physical backup, WAL archiving and PITR
Trace both NFS modes and standby backup coordination
Operate schedules, retention, logs and alerts
Measure configuration changes and prove restored correctness
Recover exact business data, change timeline and rebuild the standby

architecture.flow: Primary sends WAL to standby and repositories; pgBackRest takes coordinated standby backups into direct NFS, backup-server NFS, and S3.

boundaries: Replication also copies unwanted changes.
Both NFS modes share one NFS server.
The lab demonstrates service-outage recovery on surviving hosts, not physical host replacement.
A started database and a successful backup do not establish accepted recovery.
steps.opening_prompt: Start with the accidental-update scenario. Teach the connected concept course and its diagrams. Use hypothetical examples explicitly. Reading never grants verified lab completion.
steps.checkpoint: Read the course, ask questions, then choose Start BUILD.

teaching.brief: Set the tested data path, WAL capacity, replication limits, TLS and logging. Archiving stays off until both repository stanzas exist. Use the supplied complete contents for this file. In vi, press Escape, type :%d and Enter to clear the existing buffer, then press i and paste the contents.

configuration.body:
data_directory = '/var/lib/pgsql/16/data'
listen_addresses = '*'
port = 5432
unix_socket_directories = '/var/run/postgresql'
wal_level = replica
max_wal_senders = 5
max_replication_slots = 5
wal_keep_size = '128MB'
max_slot_wal_keep_size = '512MB'
hot_standby = on
archive_mode = off
archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=academy archive-push %p'
archive_timeout = 60
ssl = on
ssl_cert_file = 'server.crt'
ssl_key_file = 'server.key'
password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256'
logging_collector = on
log_directory = 'log'
log_filename = 'postgresql.log'
log_line_prefix = '%m [%p] '

steps.title: Write the direct UTC schedule
steps.why: The five fields are minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week. Sunday0 runs full; Monday–Saturday run differential; three daily times run incremental. Jobs on backup-1 are staggered by repository. Freshness checks and alert retries have separate short intervals. Use cron alone; do not enable duplicate systemd backup timers. Use the supplied complete contents for this file. In vi, press Escape, type :%d and Enter to clear the existing buffer, then press i and paste the contents.
steps.command_explanation: vi opens this exact file. Use the supplied complete contents for this file. In vi, press Escape, type :%d and Enter to clear the existing buffer, then press i and paste the contents. After editing, press Escape, type :wq and press Enter to save and return to Linux.
steps.expected: The editor closes and the file is saved at /tmp/pgbackrest-crontab.

verify.look_for: The exact file path is present. The following service checks establish whether its settings work.
verify.explanation: Read the observed result and compare it with the stated condition before continuing.

hints.question: What must this observation establish before the next action?
hints.hint: The editor closes and the file is saved at /tmp/pgbackrest-crontab.
hints.stronger_hint: The exact file path is present. The following service checks establish whether its settings work.

teaching.brief: The five fields are minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week. Sunday0 runs full; Monday–Saturday run differential; three daily times run incremental. Jobs on backup-1 are staggered by repository. Freshness checks and alert retries have separate short intervals. Use cron alone; do not enable duplicate systemd backup timers. Use the supplied complete contents for this file. In vi, press Escape, type :%d and Enter to clear the existing buffer, then press i and paste the contents.

configuration.body:
CRON_TZ=UTC
SHELL=/bin/bash
PATH=/usr/pgsql-16/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
MAILTO=""
0 2 * * 0 /usr/bin/python3 /opt/suta-pgbackrest/backup-job.py --config=/etc/pgbackrest/job-direct.json full >> /var/lib/suta-backup-jobs/direct/scheduler.log 2>&1
0 2 * * 1-6 /usr/bin/python3 /opt/suta-pgbackrest/backup-job.py --config=/etc/pgbackrest/job-direct.json diff >> /var/lib/suta-backup-jobs/direct/scheduler.log 2>&1
0 8,14,20 * * * /usr/bin/python3 /opt/suta-pgbackrest/backup-job.py --config=/etc/pgbackrest/job-direct.json incr >> /var/lib/suta-backup-jobs/direct/scheduler.log 2>&1
*/5 * * * * /usr/bin/python3 /opt/suta-pgbackrest/backup-job.py --config=/etc/pgbackrest/job-direct.json health >> /var/lib/suta-backup-jobs/direct/scheduler.log 2>&1
*/2 * * * * /usr/bin/python3 /opt/suta-pgbackrest/backup-job.py --config=/etc/pgbackrest/job-direct.json retry-alerts >> /var/lib/suta-backup-jobs/direct/scheduler.log 2>&1

pg1-host=pg-primary

pg1-path=/var/lib/pgsql/16/data
pg2-host=pg-standby

process-max=1
start-fast=y
archive-timeout=60
log-level-console=info
log-level-file=detail
compress-type=zst
backup-standby=y
repo2-path=/var/lib/pgbackrest/server
repo2-retention-full=2
repo3-type=s3
repo3-path={{s3_prefix}}
repo3-s3-bucket={{s3_bucket}}

repo3-s3-key-type=auto
repo3-retention-full=2

lesson_sections.title: Recover an accidental update

milestones.title: Recover an accidental update
milestones.goal: Every order amount became zero, and replication copied the mistake to the standby.
milestones.outcome: Diagnose the current attempt, repair the bounded fault, and prove protection or accepted recovery again.

scenarios.title: Recover an accidentally deleted order
scenarios.workplace_problem: Order2 disappeared. Recover to the recorded time before the delete.
boundaries: Use an isolated restore directory/port. Keep the source and forensic evidence until the recovered business data has been accepted.

After the final check, leave the accepted candidate running and send check survive in Chat. The controller verifies the result independently, then resumes saved schedules and reverses only the injected synthetic record fault. The source-service-loss exercise teaches full cutover and standby rebuilding.
hints: Start with the current job, component and timestamp.
Compare the failed component with the known healthy baseline.
Use the repair in the Guide and require a new successful backup or accepted restore.

lesson_sections.title: Recover a dropped business table

milestones.title: Recover a dropped business table
milestones.goal: A schema change dropped incident_orders. Recover it from the S3 baseline and archived WAL.
milestones.outcome: Diagnose the current attempt, repair the bounded fault, and prove protection or accepted recovery again.

scenarios.title: Reject a running database with the wrong data
scenarios.workplace_problem: The selected target is after the bad update. PostgreSQL starts, but the business data is still wrong.
boundaries: Use an isolated restore directory/port. Keep the source and forensic evidence until the recovered business data has been accepted.

After the final check, leave the accepted candidate running and send check survive in Chat. The controller verifies the result independently, then resumes saved schedules and reverses only the injected synthetic record fault. The source-service-loss exercise teaches full cutover and standby rebuilding.
hints: Start with the current job, component and timestamp.
Compare the failed component with the known healthy baseline.
Use the repair in the Guide and require a new successful backup or accepted restore.

lesson_sections.title: Reject a running database with the wrong data

milestones.title: Reject a running database with the wrong data
milestones.goal: The selected target is after the bad update. PostgreSQL starts, but the business data is still wrong.
milestones.outcome: Diagnose the current attempt, repair the bounded fault, and prove protection or accepted recovery again.

scenarios.title: A dependent backup is missing its full ancestor
scenarios.workplace_problem: A full backup was moved out of a disposable repository copy. Its dependent incremental cannot restore.
boundaries: Fault injection changes a disposable copy only. Never remove original backup or WAL objects to run this drill.

After the final check, leave the accepted candidate running and send check survive in Chat. The controller verifies the result independently, then resumes saved schedules and reverses only the injected synthetic record fault. The source-service-loss exercise teaches full cutover and standby rebuilding.
hints: Start with the current job, component and timestamp.
Compare the failed component with the known healthy baseline.
Use the repair in the Guide and require a new successful backup or accepted restore.

lesson_sections.title: The requested recovery point never existed

milestones.title: The requested recovery point never existed
milestones.goal: PostgreSQL cannot find the named point in the available WAL. A startup attempt is not a completed recovery.
milestones.outcome: Diagnose the current attempt, repair the bounded fault, and prove protection or accepted recovery again.

scenarios.title: Recover the database service and rebuild its standby
scenarios.workplace_problem: Both source database services are stopped after a later committed order. Recover the accepted earlier records, then restore normal protection.
boundaries: This proves service-outage recovery on surviving hosts, not physical host replacement. The chosen PITR point excludes the later committed order. Keep old data fenced and preserved.

After the final check, leave the accepted candidate running and send check survive in Chat. The controller verifies the result independently, then resumes saved schedules and reverses only the injected synthetic record fault. The source-service-loss exercise teaches full cutover and standby rebuilding.
hints: Start with the current job, component and timestamp.
Compare the failed component with the known healthy baseline.
Use the repair in the Guide and require a new successful backup or accepted restore.

port = 5432

lesson_sections.title: Recover the database service and rebuild its standby

milestones.title: Recover the database service and rebuild its standby
milestones.goal: Both source database services are stopped after a later committed order. Recover the accepted earlier records, then restore normal protection.
milestones.outcome: Diagnose the current attempt, repair the bounded fault, and prove protection or accepted recovery again.
